The petitioner filed this petition U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1988 for claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in RTA.
2.

The brief facts of the petitioner case are that, on 11-05- 2023 at about 4.00 p.m., he was proceeding on the two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-50/EA-1438 on left side of the NH-234 Road,
between Shidlagatta Fly Over and Anakanuru Village, Chikkaballapura, at that time, all of a sudden one Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-29/B-6969 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and without observing the traffic rules and regulations in high speed and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle and caused the accident.
Due to the accident, petitioner was fell down and sustained grievous injuries on his left leg and right hand and other parts of the body.

3. Immediately, petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Chikkaballapura for first aid and again he was shifted to Bapitist Hospital, Bangalore and further shifted to Atreum Specialty Hospital, Bangalore, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and diagnosed (1) subtrochanteric Fracture Left Femur, (2) Right Lateral end Clavicle Fracture Un-Displaced and other injuries.

The petitioner was still under treatment and bed ridden and he spent Rs.8,00,000/- towards medical,
conveyance and nourishment expenses.

Prior to the accident, the petitioner was Medical Representative at Bangalore and getting salary of Rs.28,000/- p.m. and after the accident, he is unable to do the work and suffering from loss of income.
It is further stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence driving of driver of the offending Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-29/B-6969.
In this regard, the case was registered at Chikkaballapura Traffic Police Station in Cr.No.27/2023 U/Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
Hence, respondent No.1 being the Insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
4. In pursuance to the notice, Respondent No.1 appeared before the Tribunal through its counsel filed its written statement.
The respondent No.2 did not appeared before the Tribunal and hence, he has placed as exparte.
5. Brief averments of the written statement of respondent No.1 are that, the petition is not maintainable either on facts or law.
The respondent No.1 has denied the age, income and occupation of the petitioner and also the amount spent towards medical expenses by the petitioner.

This respondent has further contended that it is the mandatory duty of the concerned police station to forward all the relevant documents to the concerned insurer within 30 days from the date of the information, but the Chikkaballapura Traffic Police Station have failed to forward the documents and not complied with the statutory demand.
It is further contended that the driver of the Lorry was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.

It is also contended that it has issued the policy in favour of the respondent No.2 in respect of the offending Lorry the liability of this respondent company if any is limited to the terms and conditions of the policy and subject to valid and effective driving licence of the driver in question and the insured vehicle had no permit and FC as on the date of the alleged accident.

It is contended that the Lorry in question did not involve in the accident nor caused accidental injuries to the petitioner, as stated in the petition or in crime records, the petitioner sustained injuries due to self fall from motorcycle, which he has riding and he was not having a valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and the petitioner in collusion with the jurisdictional police have created false records and story and lodged a false complaint.
It has further contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition against this respondent.

6. On basis of the pleadings and materials, this Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 11-05-2023 at about 4.00 p.m., he was proceeding on the two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-50/EA-1438 on left side of the NH-234 Road, between Shidlagatta Fly Over and Anakanuru Village,
Chikkaballapura, at that time, all of a sudden one Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-29/
B-6969 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering human life, came at a high speed and dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle and caused the accident.
As a result of forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
3) What order or award?

10 . Issue No.1:- The petitioner filed this petition against the respondents for claiming the compensation due to injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

16. As per spot mahazar, sketch and charge sheet it appears that, on the date of accident, the petitioner was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50/EA-1438 at left side of the Road,
between Shidlagatta Fly Over and Anakanuru Village, Chikkaballapura,

at that time, all of a sudden the offending Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-29/B-6969 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and without observing the traffic rules and regulations in high speed and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle and caused the accident. As a result of which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Hence, the Chikkaballapura Police have filed charge sheet against driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
17.
Therefore it is clear that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the offending vehicle.
For the purpose of disproving the sole negligence of the rider of the Motorcycle, nothing has been eliciting from the mouth of the petitioner.
Further, the owner of offending vehicle has not challenged the charge sheet.

18. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the petitioner has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required.
19.

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 has took the contention that the driver of the Lorry was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
The respondent No.2 has handed over the possession of the vehicle to the said driver and has contravened the proviso of MV Act and has committed the breach of the terms and conditions of the policy.

On perusal of Ex.P.5 the copy of notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act and Ex.P.6 reply to the same, it appears that, at the time of accident one Venkatesh Talavar was driving the offending Lorry and he has valid licence.
Therefore, it appears that the driver of the offending lorry was hold valid driving licence at the time of accident.

20. Further, the respondent No.1 took contention that the respondent No.2 has violated the policy terms and conditions, but the respondent No.1 has not produced oral or documentary evidence to prove its contention.
There is nothing on record to show that the respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the respondent No.1 has not proved that the respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

Hence, this Tribunal answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
22. Issue No.2:-
The petitioner claiming the compensation amount of Rs.40,00,000/- with respect to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.
The petitioner produced Wound Certificate and Discharge Summary issued by Atreum Specialty Hospital, Bangalore and prayed to award compensation amount.
The respondents not disputed the said documents.

On perusal of the wound certificate, it is discloses that the petitioner has sustained the injury as.....
1. Subtrochanteric fracture left femur.
2.Undisplaced fracture of lateral end of right clavicle.
The doctor opined that the said injuries are grievous in nature.

Therefore, taking all these facts and nature of injuries, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.60,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of pain and suffering.
23. The counsel for the petitioner argued to consider the disability of the petitioner and award the compensation to the petitioner.

Further he relied upon two citations reported in 2020 SCC Online SC 601, between Erudhaya Priya Vs. State Express Transport Corporation Ltd., and 2) 2011 ACJ 1699, between Rudra Vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Co., Ltd., & Another, for considering the disability to award of compensation.

The respondents not denied the medical bills.

On perusal of the said medical bills and also considering the bills and also treatment taken by the petitioner in the hospital, the petitioner is entitled to claim the medical bills amount of Rs.5,90,600/- under the head of medical expenditure.
25. The petitioner not produced any documents with respect to expenditure of transportation, food and other charges.
However, the petitioner produced three Discharge summaries issued by Atreum Specialty Hospital, Bangalore and Unity Lifeline Hospital (India) Pvt. Ltd., which are marked as Ex.P.10, P.26 and P.36.
It discloses that, the petitioner took treatment inpatient in the said hospitals from 12-05-2023 to 15-05-2023, 26- 11-2023 to 30-11-2023 and 25-04-2024 to 30-04-2024 i.e., for about 15 days.

Therefore, considering the treatment taken as inpatient in the hospitals, this Tribunal has award reasonable compensation of Rs.15,000/- under the head transportation, nourishment and conveyance charges.

sentences.text: The petitioner contended that, due to injuries he was suffering from pain and mental agony and he is unable to carry on his day to day activities which he used to do prior to the accident.
To prove the assessment of disability, the petitioner got examined one Doctor Shri. S.A.Somashekar as PW-4.

In the chief-examination affidavit PW.4 deposed that, on 13-02-2024 the Petitioner went to him for assessment of disability purpose and on examination he was diagnosed to have (1) subtrochanteric Fracture Left Femur and (2) Right Lateral End of Clavicle Fracture Undisplaced and he underwent ORIF with IMIL nailing for fracture left femur under SA on 12-05-2023 fracture lateral end clavicle right was treated conservatively, bone grafting plus gen-x done under SA on 28/11/2023.

Further,
the Doctor have gone through the wound certificate and discharge summary before assessing the disabilities.

The petitioner complaints of pain and difficulty to walking and climbing stairs, pain and difficulty in using right upper limb for activities of daily living, history of inability to squat and sit cross legged, history of imability to history of inability to work as medical sales representative.
O/E walks with pain and limping wasting and shortening of left lower limb is seen wasting of left upper limb is seen.
Surgical Scars are seen over left hip and thigh.

His recent X-ray No.5349 dtd:13- 02-2024 shows that (1) Non-Union fracture lateral end of right clavicle and (2) Non-union fracture subtrochanteric left femur with implants in situ and assessed the total disability of both limbs 66%
and that of the whole body at 33%.

Further deposed that the patient is said to be a Medical Representative Sales and with the said disabilities he can't carry out his work/any manual work and he needs surgery for removal of implants which would costs of Rs.1,00,000/- in private set up.

In the Cross examination admitted that, he is not the treated doctor, petitioner came on 13-02-2024 and examined him clinically and X-ray was taken on same day and not furnished radiological report for Ex.P.35 and not mentioned final figure of disability in Ex.P.34 and not taken the opinion of the treated doctor.
Further stated that, still fractures are not united as fractures complexed in nature but, wounds are healed.
Further there is only one fracture in lower limb, the clavicle fracture was undisplaced at initial stage and the surgery is not done for clavicle fracture.
The reason for non-union of both fracture is complexed fractures and lateral end of clavicle and subtrochanteric fractures.
Even for second surgery also success rate if very low and advised for second surgery disability is given by him pre-mature and another surgery is required.
However by considering the nature of the wound, condition of the petitioner and evidence of the doctor this Tribunal has considered the disability of the petitioner at 25% to the whole body.

35. Interest:
 In so far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, in MFA.No.103557/2016(between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru has held

that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest that can be awarded on Judgments cannot be more than 6% p.a. and that since Paramashivaiah N vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155939868/
9 Sec.149 of M.V. Act provides for the interest on Judgments, the interest to be awarded in claim petitions has to be 6% p.a. (excluding future medical expenses) and not more than that.

sentences.text: Hence, this Tribunal hold that the petitioner is entitled for interest @6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.
36. Liability:-
As already observed above, Respondent No.1 is the insurer and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the Lorry (Truck) bearing Reg.No.KA-29/B-6969.

As discussed in the Issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle, hence Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Further the Respondent No.1 being Insurer of the offending vehicle is primarily held liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.
Accordingly, this Tribunal is answered Issue No.2 in the Partly Affirmative.
37. Issue No.3:

For the foregoing reasons, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost as hereunder.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.18,78,600/- with interest @ 6% p.a., (excluding future medical expenses) from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 & 2 jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Further, Respondent No.1 being Insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days, from the date of this order.

18. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the petitioner has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required.

The respondent No.1 has took the contention that the driver of the Lorry was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.

On perusal of Ex.P.5 the copy of notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act and Ex.P.6 reply to the same, it appears that, at the time of accident one Venkatesh Talavar was driving the offending Lorry and he has valid licence.
Therefore, it appears that the driver of the offending lorry was hold valid driving licence at the time of accident.

There is nothing on record to show that the respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
